title: Approximate 100-Year Floodplain
description: Map of hazards in Sandy City, Utah. 828 multipolygon features, mirrored as GeoParquet in EPSG:3566 (NAD83(HARN) / Utah Central (ftUS)) with Web Mercator vector tiles for display. See the [agent guide](AGENTS.md) for the schema, the coded-value lists and queries that run.

links.title: Sandy City, Utah — Municipal Open Data
Sandy City GIS, the publisher of this layer
Licence status: Sandy City states no licence

table:columns.name: OBJECTID
table:columns.description: Esri object identifier. A row number assigned by the source geodatabase and reassigned when the layer is republished. It is not a stable key and must not be used to join across collections or across refreshes.

table:columns.name: DFIRM_ID
table:columns.description: Identifier of the Digital Flood Insurance Rate Map study this polygon belongs to.

table:columns.name: VERSION_ID
table:columns.description: Version of the FEMA database schema the record follows.

table:columns.name: FLD_AR_ID
table:columns.description: Identifier of the flood area polygon within the study.

table:columns.name: STUDY_TYP
table:columns.description: Type of flood study the mapping rests on.

table:columns.name: FLD_ZONE
table:columns.description: FEMA flood zone designation. Zone A and AE are the one-percent-annual-chance floodplain, commonly called the 100-year floodplain.

table:columns.name: ZONE_SUBTY
table:columns.description: Zone subtype. `FLOODWAY` marks the channel plus the adjoining land that must stay clear to carry the one-percent flood without raising its level.

table:columns.name: SFHA_TF
table:columns.description: Whether the polygon is a Special Flood Hazard Area. Federally backed mortgages on property here require flood insurance.

table:columns.name: STATIC_BFE
table:columns.description: Base flood elevation, the height the one-percent flood is expected to reach, where a single value applies.

table:columns.name: V_DATUM
table:columns.description: Vertical datum the elevation is measured against.

table:columns.name: DEPTH
table:columns.description: Flood depth where the zone is mapped by depth rather than elevation.

table:columns.name: LEN_UNIT
table:columns.description: Unit the elevation and depth values are in.

table:columns.name: VELOCITY
table:columns.description: Flood velocity, where measured.

table:columns.name: VEL_UNIT
table:columns.description: Unit the velocity is in.

table:columns.name: AR_REVERT
table:columns.description: Zone the area reverts to if a flood control structure is restored, for a Zone AR area behind one under repair.

table:columns.name: AR_SUBTRV
table:columns.description: Zone subtype the area reverts to.

table:columns.name: BFE_REVERT
table:columns.description: Base flood elevation the area reverts to.

table:columns.name: DEP_REVERT
table:columns.description: Depth the area reverts to.

table:columns.name: DUAL_ZONE
table:columns.description: Whether the area carries two zone designations.

table:columns.name: SOURCE_CIT
table:columns.description: Citation pointing to the study the mapping came from, within FEMA's own source table.

table:columns.name: Shape
table:columns.description: Residual Esri geometry field. It carries no coordinates here; the geometry is in the `geometry` column.

table:columns.name: Shape.STArea()
table:columns.description: Polygon area computed by the geodatabase, in the square units of the source coordinate system. Recompute it from the geometry rather than trusting it, because it is not updated when a shape is edited.

table:columns.name: Shape.STLength()
table:columns.description: Line length or polygon perimeter computed by the geodatabase, in the units of the source coordinate system. Recompute it from the geometry rather than trusting it.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Feature geometry, WKB encoded, in the collection's `proj:epsg` coordinate system.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: Per-row bounding box written by gpio, as a struct of `xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`, in the same coordinate system as the geometry. Rows are in Hilbert order, so filtering on this column prunes row groups efficiently.
